commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/knownhost.c b/src/knownhost.c
index bb5082c..0c8c2cd 100644
--- a/src/knownhost.c
+++ b/src/knownhost.c
@@ -575,8 +575,9 @@ static int knownhost_plain_match(const char *host, const char *known)
        strcmp(host_suffix, known_suffix))
         return 0;
 
-    /* the parsers work on NUL-terminated strings */
-    if(host_len >= sizeof(host_addr) || known_len >= sizeof(known_addr))
+    /* the parsers work on NUL-terminated strings; literals with a zone id
+       can grow past INET6_ADDRSTRLEN, so allow the documented maximum */
+    if(host_len > KNOWNHOST_IPV6_MAX || known_len > KNOWNHOST_IPV6_MAX)
         return 0;
 
     memcpy(host_addr, host_address, host_len);

coupling: The defect is a stack buffer overflow in knownhost_plain_match() (src/knownhost.c) that exists only as a mismatch between two bounds established by different commits. Commit 169f2b6 ('knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals') builds the matcher on fixed 46-byte scratch buffers (INET6_ADDRSTRLEN) into which the address part of each plain entry is memcpy'd before parsing, and it introduces KNOWNHOST_IPV6_MAX (64) as a documented quick-reject maximum for the text form, zone id included. In that commit the copy is correctly clamped with 'host_len >= sizeof(host_addr)' / 'known_len >= sizeof(known_addr)', so the commit alone is memory-safe and all of its own IPv6 equivalence tests pass. Commit f44ae81 ('tidy-up: miscellaneous') later relaxes exactly that copy guard to 'host_len > KNOWNHOST_IPV6_MAX || known_len > KNOWNHOST_IPV6_MAX', justified as letting literals with a zone id (which can grow past INET6_ADDRSTRLEN) reach the parser; on its own the diff reads as a harmless widening to the already-documented maximum. The overflow appears only when the two edits combine: an attacker-influenced known-hosts line whose host pattern is a colon-hex string between 47 and 64 characters long passes the relaxed macro bound and is memcpy'd into the still-46-byte stack buffers, writing up to 18 bytes past host_addr/known_addr when libssh2_knownhost_check() compares the entry. A correct fix is necessarily non-local: it must either re-tie the copy bound to the scratch size in the f44ae81 hunk or size the scratch buffers to the accepted maximum in the 169f2b6 hunk - i.e. reconcile a bound defined in one edited commit with storage defined in the other. Reading either diff in isolation shows plausible, working maintenance: with only 169f2b6's edit applied (f44ae81 left original) the over-long entry is cleanly rejected and the probe returns NOTFOUND without any sanitizer report; the bug is unreachable from that single commit alone.
